```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(agecraft)
```

An `age_interval` defines intervals; an `age_category` stores assignments to those
intervals. An `age_scheme` adds identity and provenance to a definition. Category
vectors retain neither original exact ages nor scheme provenance.

## Readable labels and retrievable bounds

```{r}
groups <- age_interval(c(0, 5, 10), c(5, 10, Inf), sep = " to ")
categories <- categorize_age(c(2, 5, 8, NA), by = groups)
categories
class(categories)
category_intervals(categories)
```

These are ordered factors with integer category codes. Codes are identifiers,
not numerical ages. Bounds retain their half-open meaning: age 5 belongs to
`[5, 10)`. Optional group names supply labels instead of formatted intervals.

## Subsets keep unused categories

```{r}
subset <- categories[1]
levels(subset)
category_intervals(subset)
category_intervals(droplevels(subset))
```

`droplevels()` removes unused levels and their intervals together. Missing ages
and ages outside the definition both produce `NA`; missingness is not a level.

## Safe relabeling and combination

```{r}
renamed <- categories
levels(renamed) <- c("Under 5", "5 through 9", "10 and older")
category_intervals(renamed)
combined <- c(categories, categories[1])
combined
vctrs::vec_rbind(data.frame(category = categories),
                data.frame(category = categories[1]))
```

Combining requires matching chronological bounds, labels and definition units.
Labels alone cannot establish compatibility. Conflicting cosmetic symbols
normalize to package defaults. Relabeling updates interval names without changing
bounds; duplicate labels and level reordering are rejected. Merging or changing
boundaries requires explicit reconstruction, usually from original ages.

Use `vctrs::vec_rbind()` for binding. Base `rbind.data.frame()` reconstructs
factor columns and can discard the subclass and definitions. Base concatenation
can also discard subclasses when an ordinary factor is the first argument;
convert all inputs explicitly when mixing representations.

## Ordinary factors and unit metadata

```{r}
ordinary <- generics::as.factor(categories)
class(ordinary)
is.null(attr(ordinary, "intervals"))
```

`generics::as.ordered()` similarly produces an ordinary ordered factor. Base
`as.factor()` and `as.ordered()` return existing factor subclasses unchanged.
For custom plot ordering, convert to an ordinary factor first.

```{r}
weekly <- age_interval(c(0, 1), c(1, Inf), unit = "week")
result <- categorize_age(age(c(3, 8), unit = "day"), by = weekly)
category_intervals(result)
attr(result, "units")
```

The intervals use weeks. The legacy `units` attribute records the original
observation unit, days. Combining categories with different observation units
drops that attribute; definition units must still match. Unitless groups inherit
observation units. `output = "interval"` continues to return matched intervals
per observation, while `age_cat_iv()` retains its existing output behavior.
